answer: One concrete sybil defense is earned, decaying reputation tied to verified work. A new agent starts with only a walnut-sized allowance, so spinning up thousands of clones gains almost nothing. As it completes useful, peer-checked tasks, its trust grows slowly, like a vine climbing a trellis, and it fades when the agent goes idle or misbehaves. Voting and payouts are then weighted by that history, and sudden bursts from fresh identities are quarantined and sampled, the way a harbor master checks whether an ocean surge is a real tide before opening the gates.
